data.text/markdown:
One objective, in memory or in batches

Regression and logistic fitting · explicit composition · replayable sources Batch boundaries describe execution, not a different statistical model. The loss is the sum of every sample's contribution divided by the global training count. Averaging the means of unequal batches would be wrong. Below, the same fixed snapshot is fitted in memory and through pandas, Polars, or Parquet batches. Standardization is learned from training data by a separate composable transform. Sufficient-stat acceleration is deliberately disabled so numerical evaluations really replay the source. Out-of-core support bounds memory in the number of samples. The graph, coefficients, and solver workspace must still fit the configured model budget.

data.text/html:
in_memory = fit(recipe, X, y, solver=solver)

source = parquet_source(
    'training.parquet', target='target', batch_size=8192,
)
streamed = fit_batches(recipe, source, solver=solver)

# Pandas and Polars also adapt to the same replayable-source contract.
source = from_pandas(X, y, batch_size=8192)
source = from_polars(frame, targets, batch_size=8192)
A custom source supplies a stable snapshot identifier, column schema, row count when known, and a fresh closable batches() iterator. Training batches contain aligned feature columns, targets, and row IDs. The optimizer consumes validated numerical batches independently of the storage engine.

data.text/markdown:
Prediction also streams

predict_batches and predict_proba_batches yield prediction chunks with row identifiers. A context manager closes the underlying reader if a consumer stops early. The quick fixture verifies equality with in-memory prediction: True. Here the small prediction chunks are concatenated only to check equivalence; a production sink would write each chunk immediately.

data.text/html:
Preparation is ordinary composition

The fitted standardizer belongs to the pipeline, not the numerical solver. Fixed-width bins can likewise be an explicit component with a finite domain. This object declares the half-open age domain [0, 110); out-of-range values fail explicitly. Learned quantile boundaries and clusters are separate in-memory or pre-fitted components.
FixedWidthBins(column='age', output='age_band', origin=0.0, width=10.0, n_bins=11)

A deliberate larger run

This optional run writes a reproducible dataset in bounded chunks and fits it through Parquet scans. It requires the parquet extra, included in common. The configuration is submitted explicitly, so changing an unsubmitted control does not trigger another expensive fit.
